$comment: Toolkit product repo: full harness adapter with strict primary-checkout edit/commit policies, plus the local Bugbot stop gate. IC workspaces ship scaffold/.cursor/hooks.json instead (cross-repo guard only). Every command is wrapped so a MULTI-ROOT Cursor session cannot deadlock: ${CURSOR_PROJECT_DIR} resolves to ONE root, which may be a repo that does not vendor .harness/ (aios-team-brain, aios-website, an IC workspace). Unwrapped, /bin/sh exits 127 (script not found) and failClosed turns that into a policy DENY, blocking every edit and shell call in the whole session. The wrapper never fails open and never over-blocks, because it decides on a MARKER FILE that identifies THIS repo specifically: scaffold/.cursor/hooks.json exists only in the toolkit checkout. Marker ABSENT means the hook does not apply to this root (exit 0); marker PRESENT but the script missing means the toolkit's own guard is broken or deleted, which is exit 3 (could-not-evaluate, mapped to a block) so enforcement is never silently lost. The marker is deliberately NOT a generic path like .cursor/hooks or .harness — an unrelated root may legitimately have those, and treating that as 'configured' would re-create the lockout. The check is inline because a helper script would sit at the same unresolvable path.

sessionStart.command: /bin/sh -c 'm="$1"; p="$2"; shift 2; [ -f "$p" ] && exec /bin/sh "$p" "$@"; [ -f "$m" ] && { echo "AIOS hook: guard is installed here but $p is missing" >&2; exit 3; }; exit 0' _ "${CURSOR_PROJECT_DIR}/scaffold/.cursor/hooks.json" "${CURSOR_PROJECT_DIR}/.harness/adapters/run-hook.sh" cursor session_start inject-context.sh
